title: 2030 三種未來：硬約束與情境分支
framing: This project treats 2030 as a near-future stress test, not a prophecy. The three versions use the same evidence base but diverge on governance, trust, energy deployment, public-sector capacity, and whether AI raises or concentrates human agency.

officialOrPrimarySources.finding: The World Economic Forum's Future of Jobs Report 2025 projects 170 million new roles and 92 million displaced roles by 2030, a net increase of 78 million jobs, alongside large-scale skill disruption.

IPCC AR6 synthesis materials state that pathways limiting warming to 1.5°C with no or limited overshoot require deep emissions cuts by 2030; this project uses that as the climate urgency boundary, not as a guaranteed outcome.
IEA renewable energy outlooks track rapid renewable capacity growth toward 2030 while emphasizing grids, permitting, supply chains, and policy as binding constraints.
The UN Sustainable Development Goals Report 2025 indicates that 2030 progress remains uneven and many targets are off track. This anchors the baseline and pessimistic public-capacity scenarios.
UN World Population Prospects 2024 provides the demographic boundary: a larger, older, and regionally divergent world by 2030, with different pressures on labor, care, migration, and urban systems.
Stanford HAI's AI Index tracks fast AI capability, adoption, investment, and policy growth. This project treats AI as a general-purpose accelerator whose social outcome depends on institutions.
WHO has warned of a projected health worker shortfall by 2030, especially in low- and lower-middle-income regions. This informs the care-system pressure in all three scenarios.

optimistic.name: 樂觀版：協調成功
optimistic.logic: AI becomes civic infrastructure rather than a private race. Renewables, grids, adaptation, care work, and education scale together. Institutions audit models, protect labor mobility, and use data for public capacity.
optimistic.warning: Even optimistic 2030 is not solved; it is only less brittle.

baseline.name: 一般版：局部適應
baseline.logic: Most places adopt AI and clean energy, but institutions move unevenly. Productivity rises in pockets, old infrastructure remains, labor stress persists, and public systems spend much of 2030 doing triage.
baseline.warning: This is the default path if progress continues but coordination remains partial.

pessimistic.name: 悲觀版：碎片化失控
pessimistic.logic: AI amplifies inequality and information disorder, climate shocks exceed adaptation capacity, grids and public systems become brittle, and trust collapses into defensive fragmentation.
pessimistic.warning: This path is not inevitable, but it is reachable through delay, extraction, and institutional decay.

creativeThesis: 2030 is not one destination. It is a fork made visible: the same technologies can widen human agency, patch a strained system, or accelerate fragmentation.
